Pasta & Bean Soup With Cabbage {Pasta e Fagioli}

By Deborah  •  November 16, 2026
⌄  Jump to Recipe
Listen to audio version of this article
Instaread
Sponsored by

Pasta e fagioli is the kind of soup I make when the weather turns and I want something that fills the kitchen with a good smell. This version adds cabbage, and it makes the pot even heartier. Carrots, celery, onion and garlic start things off in olive oil with diced pancetta, which gives the broth a savory, slightly smoky backbone. Then come chopped tomatoes, chicken broth and two cans of creamy cannellini beans, with short dried pasta tucked in at the end. I prefer tubetti or ditalini pasta for this recipe, but I had neither available when I wanted to make this pasta dish. Instead I made do with small shells which worked out just fine.

The cabbage softens into silky ribbons that add a gentle sweetness and a little extra body to every spoonful. It’s thick, comforting and very much a one-bowl meal. Ladle it out and top it generously with grated Parmesan.

My husband likes to serve this soup over a thick, crusty slice of toasted Italian bread, but I prefer the soup just as it is! Leftovers are even better the next day, but the pasta will keep absorbing broth in the fridge, so add a splash of broth or water when you reheat it. The pasta will not be “al dente” unless you cook the pasta separately and add it to the dish at the very end.

Pasta Fagioli with Cabbage

yield: 6-8prep time: 20 MINUTEScook time: 45 MINUTEStotal time: 1 HOUR 5 MINUTES

Hearty pasta fagioli with cabbage, pancetta, cannellini beans and short pasta, finished with Parmesan. A cozy, comforting soup for cold weather.

Print
Table of Contents
  • Ingredients
  • Instructions
  • Notes
  • Did you make this recipe?

Ingredients ● Cook Mode

  • 2 Tablespoons Extra Virgin Olive Oil, Plus More For Drizzling
  • 4 Ounces Diced Pancetta
  • 1 Large Yellow Onion, Chopped
  • 2 Medium Carrots, Peeled And Diced
  • 2 Stalks Celery, Diced
  • 4 Cloves Garlic, Minced
  • 1/2 Small Head Green Cabbage (About 1 Pound), Cored And Thinly Sliced Or Chopped
  • 1 Can (14.5 Ounces) Chopped Tomatoes, With Their Juices
  • 6 Cups Chicken Broth, Plus More As Needed
  • 2 Cans (15 Ounces Each) Cannellini Beans, Drained And Rinsed
  • 1 Cup Ditalini Pasta (Small Shells Or Tubetti Also Work)
  • Salt And Freshly Ground Black Pepper, To Taste
  • Freshly Grated Parmesan Cheese, For Serving

Instructions

  1. 1Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy soup pot over medium heat. Add the diced pancetta and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the fat has rendered and the pieces are lightly golden but not crisp.
  2. 2Add the onion, carrots, and celery along with a good pinch of salt. Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until the vegetables are soft and the onion looks translucent.
  3. 3Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute, just until fragrant.
  4. 4Add the cabbage and stir to coat it in the pan drippings. Cook for 5 minutes, until it begins to wilt and shrink down.
  5. 5Pour in the chopped tomatoes with their juices and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes darken slightly and smell sweet.
  6. 6Pour in the chicken broth and add the cannellini beans. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to a gentle simmer.
  7. 7Cover partially and cook for 15 minutes, until the cabbage is very tender. For a creamier, thicker broth, use the back of a spoon to mash about 1/2 cup of the beans against the side of the pot.
  8. 8Taste the soup and season with salt and pepper. Stir in the ditalini and raise the heat so the soup returns to a steady simmer.
  9. 9Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often so the pasta doesn't stick to the bottom, until the pasta is al dente (tender with a slight bite). The pasta will absorb roughly 1 cup of the broth as it cooks, so the soup will thicken from brothy to hearty and stew-like. If it looks too thick for your liking, stir in another 1/2 to 1 cup of broth or water.
  10. 10Remove the pot from the heat and let the soup rest for 5 minutes. Ladle into warm bowls, drizzle each with a little olive oil, and top generously with freshly grated Parmesan and a few grinds of black pepper.

Notes

Tips
• Thin leftovers as needed. Pasta keeps absorbing liquid as the soup sits, so add a splash of broth or water when reheating to loosen it.
• Add a Parmesan rind. If you have one, drop it into the pot along with the broth and beans and remove it before serving. It adds a deep, savory flavor.
• Cook the pasta in the soup or separately. Cooking it in the soup gives a silkier, thicker broth. If you plan on leftovers, cook the pasta separately in salted water, then add it to each bowl as you serve so it doesn't turn soft in storage.
Storage
Cool the soup completely, then refrigerate in an airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat gently on the stove over medium-low heat, adding broth or water to thin it. For longer storage, freeze the soup without the pasta for up to 3 months, then thaw overnight in the refrigerator, bring it to a simmer, and add freshly cooked pasta.
